model_answer: Private data, untrusted content and exfiltration. A config reader opens private data: it returns a token the model can see. A page fetcher opens untrusted content: someone outside wrote the text. A report or post tool opens exfiltration: it sends data to a host the attacker can reach. With all three open, an instruction in the page can make the agent read the token and send it out. Cutting any one leg breaks the attack.
prompt: Name the three legs of the lethal trifecta, and give one tool that opens each.
rubric: Names all three legs: private data, untrusted content and exfiltration
Gives one tool for each leg
Says that all three open together is the risk
Says that cutting one leg breaks the attack

model_answer: The sentence is text the model reads, so it lowers the rate at which the model obeys an injected instruction. It does not remove a leg. A control in the harness does: an egress allow-list the send cannot pass, a deny rule on the outbound call, or no untrusted content in reach. The model may still follow the injected text, so the defense has to make the send fail whatever the model decides.
prompt: Why is a sentence in the system prompt not enough to stop an injected page? What would be enough?
rubric: Says the wording lowers the rate and removes no leg
Names one harness control that cuts a leg
Says the model may still follow injected text, so the defense must hold then
Says that a control the model cannot argue with is what makes the send fail
